summary: The note surveys security challenges posed by the rapid growth of Internet of Things (IoT) devices, which passed 30 billion active units by mid-September 2023. It covers risks such as neglected updates, lack of standardization and weak authentication, along with mitigations including encryption, AI-based anomaly detection, user education, supply chain vetting, regulation and industry collaboration. It concludes that a secure IoT ecosystem requires continuous collective effort from manufacturers, developers, policymakers and users.
one_line: Overview of IoT security risks in 2023 and the encryption, authentication, AI, regulation and collaboration efforts aimed at addressing them.
key_facts: TechAdvancer reported that by mid-September 2023 the number of active IoT devices surpassed 30 billion.
Dr. Maria Reynolds said "each new device represents a potential entry point for security breaches."
Jason Becker, a software engineer specializing in IoT systems, said many IoT devices are built with cost and convenience in mind, often at the expense of security.
The Global IoT Council convened on November 10, 2023 to discuss frameworks for a cohesive approach to IoT security, because lack of standardization is a major hurdle.
Rebecca Hughes, a senior security analyst, said on October 15, 2023 that without strong encryption IoT devices are "low-hanging fruit for cybercriminals."
NextGen Security showcased a new line of IoT locks using biometric recognition at the Consumer Tech Show on October 3, 2023.
IoTSecure has begun rolling out automatic update systems so its devices stay protected against emerging threats.
Sophia Zhang, an AI researcher, demonstrated on September 29, 2023 how machine learning can analyze network traffic patterns to identify anomalies indicative of a cyber attack.
CyberWise has launched initiatives to inform the public about best practices for IoT security.
CyberGuard Alliance published a report on November 20, 2023 highlighting hidden risks in the IoT supply chain and sparking discussion of rigorous security audits.
The Internet of Secure Things Act, introduced in the U.S. Congress on December 1, 2023, seeks to mandate changeable passwords and the ability to receive security patches.
Leading tech companies formed the IoT Security Coalition on September 22, 2023 to develop shared security protocols and respond to threats collectively.
